live in `apply_payfast_itn()` - NOT fixed this pass, flagged for Sarel's own call.** Orientation:
`git fetch origin main` showed no new commits since this routine's own last pass (`fd30549`) -
local checkout confirmed on the real tip (`git rev-parse HEAD` == `git rev-parse origin/main`)
before starting, per the standing habit this routine adopted after getting burned by a stale
checkout twice. Collision check: only open PR is `#118` (draft, stale, unrelated); every other
branch on the remote is an orphaned, already-merged source branch. Stayed entirely clear of the PR
#143/#149/#150 (and #131/#134-#138/#142) self-merge incident, as directed - that's in Sarel's own
hands across two parallel conversations.

**The finding**: `apply_payfast_itn()` (0078, last redefined in `0083`) has no idempotency guard
against a duplicate/redelivered ITN for the SAME payment. Reproduced live against a fresh replay of
all 87 migrations on a scratch Postgres: called it once for a test company with
`p_payment_status='COMPLETE'` and a `p_period_end` of "now + 1 month" (mirroring the real route
handler, `app/api/billing/payfast/itn/route.ts`, which recomputes `nextPeriodEnd()` fresh from
`Date.now()` on every single invocation, with no memory of any prior call) - `current_period_end`
set correctly to one month out. Called it again immediately after, with the exact same
`m_payment_id`/`pf_payment_id`/`'COMPLETE'` status (simulating a genuine webhook redelivery, which
PayFast's own docs describe as something a merchant's endpoint must tolerate) but computed as if 10
days had passed - `current_period_end` silently moved another 10 days further out, with no new
payment having occurred. The route handler itself always acks PayFast with `200 OK` regardless of
outcome specifically so PayFast won't retry-on-failure, which rules out the most common cause of
duplicate delivery, but doesn't rule out PayFast's own infrastructure-level redelivery, which is
exactly the scenario their own ITN docs warn integrators to handle idempotently.

**Why this needs Sarel's own call, not a straight fix in this pass**: the honest, correct fix isn't
small. `m_payment_id` (our own merchant-generated id, stored on the subscription row) stays
constant across a RECURRING subscription's whole lifetime in PayFast's model, while `pf_payment_id`
(their own id) is meant to be unique PER CHARGE - so the dedup key has to be `pf_payment_id`, not
`m_payment_id`, or every legitimate monthly renewal charge would get silently swallowed as a "dupe"
of the first one. That needs a new claim/dedup table (the same shape this codebase already uses
elsewhere for exactly this problem - `sent_deadline_reminders`, `sent_operational_alerts`,
`notification_claims` from 0093), not a one-line guard, and I haven't independently confirmed
PayFast's exact subscription-ITN field semantics against their own docs/SDK the way `lib/payfast.ts`'s
existing code clearly already did for the signature algorithm - getting this wrong in the wrong
direction (treating a legitimate renewal as a dupe) would silently stop a paying customer's renewal
from ever taking effect, which is worse than the bug it would fix. **Not urgent today**: this repo's
own migration `0083` header confirms no live Supabase project has ever run this schema yet, and
`lib/payfast.ts`'s own header confirms PayFast is sandbox-only, Sarel's own explicit instruction -
there is no live money or a real recurring customer this can affect right now. Flagging it here
rather than rushing a fix that could get the dedup key wrong, especially with two other migrations
(`0096`, `0097`) already queued waiting on Sarel's own apply step - a third, money-adjacent one isn't
something this pass should add without him seeing it first.

this pass - the reproduction above was done entirely against a scratch Postgres, nothing in the

**The finding**: the 2026-10-17 cross-tenant-integrity audit (migration `0043`,
docs/specs/POPIA-Security-Audit.md) attached a `tt_same_company` trigger to every tenant table with
a `tender_id` column, so a company can only ever reference a tender it can actually see (shared, or
its own private one) - never another company's private tender by UUID alone, even though RLS itself
has no opinion on that (`is_company_member(company_id)` only checks whose row it is, never what the
row points at). `narrative_documents` (migration `0087`, the cover-letter/methodology generator) has
exactly that same shape - `company_id` + `tender_id` - but was added 44 migrations after the audit
and was never given the guard every sibling table already has (`tender_tasks`, `tender_packs`,
`tender_answers`, `financial_captures`, `generated_documents`, `generated_cvs`,
`pack_generation_jobs`, `tender_comments`, `tender_private_documents`).

Reproduced live, not assumed: replayed all 96 migrations onto a scratch Postgres
(`engine/security/replay_schema.sh`, clean exit), created two companies and a PRIVATE tender owned
by company B, confirmed `tt_tender_visible_to()` itself correctly says company A cannot see it, then
inserted a `narrative_documents` row as company A pointing `tender_id` straight at B's private
tender - the insert succeeded. Real impact, same shape 0043's own header already describes for every
table it covers: the always-on worker (service role, bypasses RLS by design) reads the referenced
tender's own buyer/description/closing-date to ground the AI-drafted text, so a company holding only
B's tender UUID (not a secret - a URL in a screenshot or an old e-mail is enough, 0043's own stated
threat model) could confirm a private tender exists and pull its details into its own generated
document. It would also pollute `narrative_documents_tender_kind_ready_idx`, the exact index the
anti-collusion similarity check (0087's own stated reason for existing) queries across every

**2026-10-24 ~23:07 UTC — PR #148 merged (`f6cd4e7`); live verification dispatch of `founder-digest.yml`/`scout-alerts.yml` ran, both exited 0, but every notification attempt inside both failed at `claim_notification` - zero emails actually sent.** Sarel: migrations `0094`/`0095` applied to the live DB, merge PR #148, dispatch the two Resend-only workflows as a real end-to-end test. Both dispatched via `workflow_dispatch`, both jobs completed with `conclusion: success` (the script's own top-level `main()` didn't throw) - but reading the actual job logs shows every single `sendNotification()` call inside both scripts failed before ever reaching Resend:

```
claim_notification failed for founder-digest-2026-10-25 { code: 'PGRST202', message: 'Could not find the function public.claim_notification(p_idempotency_key, p_notification_type) in the schema cache' }
Founder daily digest (25 Oct 2026): failed.

Quality Scout anomaly alerts: 0 sent, out of 15 candidate(s) (47 open alert(s) total).
```

`PGRST202` is PostgREST's "this function isn't in my schema cache" error - distinct from "the function doesn't exist in Postgres at all". `claim_notification`/`record_notification_sent` are migration `0093`'s own functions (part of PR #145, merged earlier this session) - **not** `0094`/`0095` (those only add `company_notification_recipients`, which neither `founder-digest.yml` nor `scout-alerts.yml` even calls - they don't read company recipients at all, so this run did not actually exercise `0094`/`0095` either way). Two honest possibilities, not distinguishable from this sandbox: (a) migration `0093` itself was never applied to the live DB (only `0094`/`0095` were, per Sarel's own message - those two don't depend on `0093` existing, so they could have been applied cleanly even with `0093` still missing), or (b) `0093` is applied but PostgREST's schema cache is stale and needs a reload - a well-known Supabase gotcha when SQL is run directly via the dashboard SQL editor instead of `supabase db push` (the fix is either waiting ~60s for the automatic reload, or Settings → API → "Reload schema", or `NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';`).

**Net result, stated plainly: the live verification test did not confirm delivery - it confirmed the opposite.** Zero emails were sent by either run; there is no Resend delivery ID to report, because `sendTransactionalEmail()` is never reached when `claim_notification` fails first. Not a new code bug - the same migration-application gap this file already flagged twice (migration `0094`'s own entry, and the "no CI step applies migrations" note). Waiting on Sarel to confirm `0093` is live and the PostgREST schema cache is fresh before re-dispatching.

`tender-workspace-batch-2b`), marked ready for review after live verification - not self-merged.

- **`assess_tender.py`'s `labels()` helper used to append the raw taxonomy slug in parens after
  every discipline label** (`"Generators & Backup Power (generators_backup_power)"`) - a debugging
  artifact that reached real `/discovery` copy. Fixed at the root (the helper itself, plus one
  reason string that bypassed it entirely). **Caveat for any session checking this live**:
  `opportunities.reasons` is written once by the discovery pipeline (`watch_new_tenders.py` →
  `assess_fit()`), not recomputed on page render - the live preview still shows the *old* leaked
  text for every already-scraped opportunity until the daily discovery run reassesses it. Confirmed
  via `test_taxonomy.py`'s real regression fixtures that the fix itself is correct; did not force a
  production rescrape to prove it live (that's a real side-effecting action against the shared
  database and real government sites, out of scope for a text-copy fix).
- **4 sources (Rand Water, Kouga, Vaal Central Water, Lephalale) confirmed date-only, never a time**
  for their closing date - `parse_sast()`'s generic midnight default then displayed as a literal
  "00:00". Added `iso_sast_closing()` (`source_http.py`), used only at these 4 call sites, defaulting
  to 11:00 SAST - the generic `iso_sast()`/`parse_sast()` is untouched since it also backs
  `published_date` everywhere, where midnight is a harmless marker, not a fabricated deadline. Same
  go-forward-only caveat as above applies to already-stored rows.
- **`<html lang="en-ZA">` does NOT control the native `<input type="date">` picker's display
  order - tested directly, confirmed wrong, don't repeat this assumption.** The brief asked for SA
  dd/mm/yyyy date inputs instead of US mm/dd/yyyy; the obvious-looking fix (set the document's own
  `lang`) was tried, verified empirically (an isolated `lang="en"` vs `lang="en-ZA"` date input, same
  value, screenshotted - both rendered `01/15/2026`), and found not to work. A browser's native date
  picker format follows the *browser's own UI language setting*, not the page's `lang` attribute -
  confirmed by Chrome's own engineering FAQ (no standard web-author hook exists for this at all).
  `lang="en-ZA"` is still in the PR (harmless, correct for other reasons - accessibility, spellcheck,
  `Intl` calls) but does not achieve the stated goal. A real fix needs a custom date-input component
  (text input + mask, replacing the native control) across 4 date fields - flagged as a scoped
  follow-up for Sarel's own call, not built speculatively.

**Tender Command Center & Operational Logistics Engine - merged to `main` as PR #132
(`576914e`), real data confirmed working - 2026-10-23/24.** Full response to Sarel's own brief
of the same name: the dashboard's "Closing soon" list is replaced with a real operational-triage
view built around South African public-tender physical-submission logistics (printing, binding,
transit all take real hours, and the real cutoff for a physical box is `closing_date -
print_hours - transit_hours`, well before the tender's own closing time).

- **Migration 0090** adds 6 columns to `tender_packs`: `submission_type`, `delivery_location`,
  `estimated_transit_hours` (default 2), `estimated_print_hours` (default 4), `dispatch_status`
  (6-value enum, default `not_ready`), `courier_contact`. Replayed clean (80 migrations) and
  tenant-isolation-tested (`engine/security/test_tenant_isolation.py` → ALL PASSED). No new RLS
  policy needed - the existing `tender_packs` tenant-isolation policy already covers every new
  column.
- **Deliberately NOT stored, by design**: `print_sign_deadline` and `blocking_items` are both
  computed on read (`lib/dispatchTriage.ts`), never columns - the same "never a second number that
  could disagree" rule this app already follows everywhere (`compliance-report.tsx`,
  `tender-readiness.ts`). `decision_needed` is scoped to the 2 of 4 values with a real signal
  anywhere in this schema (`attend_briefing`, `director_resolution`) - `GO_NO_GO` and
  `PRICING_SIGNOFF` are not implemented, not fabricated: no sign-off workflow exists anywhere in
  this app today (`financial_captures`, migration 0001, is still just draft/complete).
- **Pure triage logic** (`lib/dispatchTriage.ts`) is unit-tested in isolation - 20 tests
  (`dispatchTriage.test.ts`), covering the deadline arithmetic, the 4-bucket priority order, and
  the decision-derivation edge cases (a fix-blocker more than 7 days out is still `none`; a past
  briefing never fires `attend_briefing` again).
- **Dashboard** (`app/dashboard/page.tsx`, `lib/dispatchDashboard.ts`, `components/tt/command-
  center.tsx`): Zone 1 critical banner (single highest-urgency tender, honestly absent when
  nothing's at risk - not a disguised "all clear"), 3-lane Zone 2 (Needs decision / Urgent actions
  & blocked items / Dispatch & delivery), Zone 3 Radar collapsed by default. Every card reuses the
  already-proven `lib/tenderNextStep.ts`'s `nextStepFor()` for its blocking-item summary - no

**Real bug, only surfaced once migration 0090 was applied to real data, found and fixed before
merge.** Re-verified the preview immediately after Sarel confirmed the migration was applied: the
dashboard now threw to its generic whole-page `ErrorState` (not the soft `{error}` banner from
before) - a genuine crash, not graceful degradation. Root cause: `renderDashboard()`'s new
`activeBids` builder filtered on `IN_PROGRESS_STAGES.includes(stageOf(t))`, and `stageOf()` falls
back to `"found"` (itself an in-progress stage) for any tender with **no `tender_packs` row at
all** (i.e. every opportunity nobody has clicked "Start a tender pack" on yet) - so
`t.tender_packs[0].id` read `.id` off `undefined` and crashed the whole page the moment this
company had any not-yet-started tender in its pipeline (this test account had 7). Only showed up
with real data because the pre-migration preview's own `{error}` banner masked it entirely (the
`tenders` select itself was failing first, before `activeBids` ever ran). Fixed by filtering on
`tender_packs.length > 0` before building triage cards - a tender with no pack yet has nothing
real to triage anyway, consistent with the feature's own premise. Re-verified clean on the live
preview after the fix: dashboard's 3 lanes populate correctly (7 active bids, one real Dispatch &
delivery card with a working tap-to-advance `DispatchStatusButton`), the workspace's
`SubmissionModeBadge` shows the real Closing time / − transit / − print & bind / Hard target
breakdown, the Pack compiler tab's logistics form saves correctly - all with zero console errors.
Full local suite re-run green after the fix (tsc/eslint/build/vitest 147/147/node-test 138/138).

**I was wrong two passes ago, and should say so plainly rather than let it stand**: the `httpx`
`ModuleNotFoundError` in `engine/cv/test_extract_cv_fields.py` and
`engine/onboarding/test_classify_documents.py` was recorded here as "a confirmed sandbox-only
gap... will pass there [the real worker container]". That was wrong. Checking the **real**
`bridge-worker-ci` run on `main` (the one from PR #126's own merge, `305f29c`, which predates PR
#74 and proves this isn't something PR #74 caused) shows the identical failure in real GitHub
Actions CI, not just this sandbox - confirmed by reading that run's own job log and its own `pip
install` output directly. The real root cause: `anthropic==1.15.0`'s own real dependency is
`httpx2<3,>=2.0.0`, not `httpx` - confirmed from `anthropic/_base_client.py`'s own import lines and
its own docstring ("`httpx` objects don't work with `httpx2`, and would otherwise fail deep inside
a request"). A bare `import httpx` in those two tests was wrong twice over: nothing in this
dependency tree ever installs plain `httpx`, and even if it did, handing an `httpx.Response` to
`anthropic.BadRequestError` would silently misbehave per that same docstring, not just fail to
import. **Fixed**: `import httpx2 as httpx` in both files - minimal, re-verified clean (both
files individually, full 55-file Python sweep). This is real CI-red on `main` that predates PR #74
(confirmed on `305f29c`, the commit before it), not caused by the merge just performed.
**Confirmed in real CI, not just locally**: both `app-ci` and `bridge-worker-ci` are green on
`main`'s current tip (`c71c17e`) - the fix verified against the actual GitHub Actions run, not
assumed from the local sweep alone.

**Standing review pass, 2026-10-23 ~14:20 UTC: a real test-suite break found and fixed on `main`
itself, root cause confirmed before touching anything (Finding 62).** Since the last pass: PR
#117 merged (SANRAL-mention fix, already checked for overlap with PR #74 last pass - none) and
Finding 61 (ambiguous closing-time/delivery-address flagging in `engine/intake/classify_tender.py`
- touches `engine/general/`, `engine/intake/`, no overlap with PR #74). Merged forward cleanly;
while re-running the full Python sweep straight after, `engine/discovery/test_randwater.py` failed
for the first time this session: `is_closed computed correctly from the real closing date (future
-> not yet closed)` asserted `False` but got `True`.

**Root-caused before fixing, not just re-run hoping it was a fluke**: this test's `FIXTURE_PAGE` is
a real, frozen snapshot of Rand Water's own bids page (captured by Sarel 2026-10-20), and every one
of its 4 real bids has a real closing date of `23 Oct 2026 16:00 SAST`. `is_closed` is computed via
`source_http.is_past()` against the real wall clock (`datetime.now()`), not a fixed/frozen time -
so the test's own assertion was correct on 2026-10-20 (closing date still in the future) and
necessarily, permanently wrong from the moment the real clock crossed 2026-10-23 16:00 SAST
onward, which happened mid-session today. Not a flake, not caused by anything this pass or any
other session changed - the code (`is_past()`) was computing the honest, correct answer the whole
time; the test's own frozen expectation simply aged past its own fixture's real date. Confirmed by
reproducing the identical failure on a clean `main` checkout before writing any fix, not assumed
from one failing run.

**Fix**: flipped the assertion to `is True` with an explanatory comment (the closing date is a
fixed point in time that has now passed and will stay passed) - not a workaround, not a skip, the
simple truth once real time caught up to this fixture's own real date. Re-ran the full repo-wide
Python sweep after: 51/51 files, 0 failures.

**Worth flagging for whoever next touches this test file**: any fixture with a hardcoded near-term
real date will eventually flip the same way, on whatever day the fixture's own date arrives - this
is not specific to Rand Water or to today. Not fixing that general pattern here (it would mean
auditing every such fixture across the discovery test suite, a separate, broader task), just
naming it so the next person who hits one of these doesn't have to re-derive the same reasoning
from scratch.

2026-10-23 ~00:30 UTC - retrofitted, not just flagged.** `docs/specs/AI-Call-Quality-Standard.md`
(merged into `main` while PR #74 was still open, see the entry below) is Sarel's own standing
rule, verbatim: "neve be stisfied with your first anser and output, always review it... run that
3 times." `engine/narrative/generate_narrative.py` is exactly the kind of call this targets - it
generates a document that goes into a real tender submission - and it was single-pass. Rather than
merge PR #74 with a known gap against a standard that landed the same day, retrofitted it for real:

- **`run_review_passes()`** (new, `generate_narrative.py`) chains up to 3 real self-review turns
  onto the SAME conversation the draft was generated in - a genuine multi-turn exchange (the
  model's own prior output as a real assistant turn, not a reconstructed prompt pretending to be
  one), using the literal review-prompt template the standard specifies. Stops the moment a pass
  reports nothing wrong; if the model is still finding (and fixing) real issues on the very last
  allowed pass, `quality_flagged` comes back true - the same honest-flag discipline
  `similarity_flagged` already uses, so a human decides rather than the system assuming the last
  attempt was good enough.
- **`call_llm()` generalized** to accept either a bare string (back-compatible, wrapped into a
  single-turn message) or a real multi-turn messages list, and a per-call `schema` (generation
  calls use the existing `output_schema()`; review calls use the new `review_output_schema()`,
  which adds `no_issues_found`/`review_notes` without changing the `sections` shape downstream
  code already depends on). Now returns the full parsed dict, not just `sections` - callers that
  need the review-specific fields can read them; existing callers just read `parsed["sections"]`.
- **Migration `0086_narrative_documents.sql` edited in place** (not a new migration) to add
  `quality_review_passes`/`quality_flagged` columns - safe since this table has never been applied
  anywhere real (PR #74 still unmerged; confirmed no collision with `main`'s current migration
  numbering, still ends at `0086`). `process_narrative_jobs.py` persists both; the Tender Workspace
  card (`narrative-documents.tsx`) shows a plainly-worded amber warning banner when
  `quality_flagged` is true, same visual pattern as the existing red similarity-flagged banner -
  "never present an output that failed its own quality check as if it passed" meant the UI, not
  just the database row, had to actually show it.
- **Real test coverage, not just "it compiles"**: `test_generate_narrative.py` proves the loop
  stops early on a clean pass, chains corrections into the next pass's actual input (not the
  original draft), caps at exactly 3 passes and flags honestly if still finding issues on the
  last one, and sends a genuine multi-turn conversation (asserted against the real messages array
  the stub client received) - not just that the function runs without error. Found and fixed one
  real stub-harness bug along the way: `StubClient` was storing a reference to the mutable
  `messages` list, not a snapshot, so later appends in the production code were leaking backward
  into an earlier call's recorded state - a test-only bug (the real Anthropic SDK serializes the
  request before returning), but a real bug in the test, caught by writing a test specific enough
  to notice it, not assumed away.
- **Re-verified everything after the retrofit**: fresh 76-migration replay (clean), full
  tenant-isolation suite (`ALL PASSED`), all 5 `engine/narrative/test_*.py` files (0 failures,
  including the new review-pass and schema tests), `npm run verify` clean.

**Not done**: no real LLM call exercises this loop end to end (same standing sandbox limitation as
everything else in this feature - no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` here). The review loop runs strictly
*after* the uniqueness distinctness-retry settles, not interleaved with or re-checked against it -
a deliberate ordering choice (documented in the function's own docstring) to avoid the two checks
chasing each other, not an oversight. `docs/specs/AI-Call-Quality-Standard.md`'s own text names
three *other*, pre-existing call sites (`company_documents.py`, `extract_cv_fields.py`,
`classify_documents.py`) as still single-pass, explicitly calling that separate follow-up work -
this pass only retrofitted the one call site it was already touching.

`app/app/signup/page.tsx`).** Closes the gap flagged throughout this file since 2026-10-18:
Supabase's Azure OAuth provider had Google's credentials pasted into it by mistake, so
`MICROSOFT_AUTH_READY` existed as a `false` flag to hide the "Continue with Microsoft" button
rather than expose that broken path to a real visitor.

Sarel registered a real Microsoft Entra app, walked through step by step and verified together
rather than just reported as done:

  account users") - deliberately NOT the default single-tenant option, which would have only
  allowed `clev.co.za` accounts to sign in rather than any customer's Microsoft account. This is
  the one step in the whole flow that's easy to get wrong silently (the default selection looks
  reasonable and would have shipped a Microsoft SSO button that fails for every real customer).
- **Redirect URI**: Supabase's own `https://swkglctgdceqrehbabfl.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback`.

  approaches should either rotate it proactively or expect Microsoft SSO to silently start failing
  for every user the day it lapses (Azure doesn't warn end users, only shows in the Azure Portal
  app registration's own Certificates & secrets page).
- **Supabase side** (Authentication → Providers → Azure): real Client ID + Client Secret pasted in
  (replacing Google's mistakenly-pasted ones), Tenant field set to
  **`https://login.microsoftonline.com/common`** to match the multi-tenant registration - note this
  field validates as a URL, not a bare tenant name like `common` alone (caught live during setup,
  first attempt was rejected).

Also closed in the same pass: `signup/page.tsx` never had Google/Microsoft OAuth at all (only
email/password, ported late and separately) - added via PR #90, same `MICROSOFT_AUTH_READY` gate,
merged before this one.

**Open, not this pass's to fix**: the orange Azure Portal warning on the app registration -
"End users cannot grant consent to newly registered multitenant apps without verified
publishers" - some companies with stricter Microsoft tenant consent policies may need their own IT
admin to approve before staff can use "Continue with Microsoft". Fixing it means Microsoft Partner
Network (MPN) publisher verification, a separate optional step, not required for this to work for
most users today.

**One minor residual edge case, worth naming but not worth fixing now**: the rescue path updates
`status`/`payfast_token`/`current_period_end` but never touches `payfast_m_payment_id` itself. If a
company starts checkout A (plan X), then checkout B (plan Y) before A's ITN arrives, and A's `COMPLETE`
ITN is rescued, the subscription activates - but still under whatever plan `company_subscriptions`
currently holds (B's selection, since `start_payfast_checkout()` writes plan/interval immediately,
before payment). If B then fails, `apply_payfast_itn()` would set `past_due` even though A's payment
genuinely succeeded. This requires two *overlapping* checkout attempts for *different plans* inside
one ITN round-trip - a real but narrow edge case, strictly rarer than the one Finding 51 already fixed
(which just needed two attempts, same or different plan, in either order). Not fixed here - flagging
for whoever next touches this function, not urgent enough to justify touching money-adjacent code on
a standing review pass alone.

- `submission-plan-logic.ts` covers only what had no existing classifier to reuse - forms,

  Review already says about the exact same document or role.
- **Real decision, checked against evidence before deciding (not a guess):** `FORM_STATUS_STYLE`
  (`lib/generalTender.ts`) already colors `by_hand` forms AMBER ("Complete by hand"), the same color
  as Provide - not red/Fix. So `by_hand` -> `needs_input`/Provide here too, not `missing`/Fix as a
  first instinct might suggest (a form needing manual completion isn't itself a disqualification
  risk, it's work only a person can do - matches Provide's own AGENTS.md definition exactly).
  `auto`/`attach`/`overlay` -> `confirmed`/Verify (already styled green). Buyer forms follow the same
  rule (overlay -> Verify, else -> Provide).
- **CIDB grading comparison** (separate from the "cidb" returnable): no grading on file at all ->
  `missing`/Fix (nothing to even compare); grading on file -> `needs_input`/Provide, NOT
  `confirmed`/Verify - the engine admits it can't compare grading codes itself, so a human must
  actually do the comparison, same reasoning `localityStatus()`'s own "unknown" case already uses.
- **Compulsory briefing** -> always `needs_input`/Provide (an action only a person can physically
  do - never Verify, nothing was filled; never Fix, it's not a document/data gap).
- **Gaps** (the engine admitting it couldn't confidently determine something, after de-duplicating
  against each by_hand/overlay form's own restated gap message, ported faithfully from
  `submission_plan.py`'s own `_form_gap_prefixes`) -> `missing`/Fix - a real unresolved risk, unlike
  a by_hand form where the engine succeeded and the task is simply known.
- `submission-plan-data.ts` mirrors `general-pack-review-data.ts`'s own conventions exactly
  (`cache()`-wrapped, per-section try/catch, same Supabase queries for company/tender_answers/

**`submission_plan.py` added, 2026-10-21 ~10:30 UTC: first version of the "assessment engine"**
Sarel asked for ("assesses each tender, each page, each field and compiles a plan of how to
prepare a submission", `fb7b2ba`). `compile_plan(manifest, company, tender)` is a pure function
(no Supabase access, same discipline as `requirements.py` itself) that turns the existing
requirement manifest into an ordered, actionable list: one step per form/buyer-form/returnable/
role/question/CIDB-grading/briefing, each with a status (ready / needs_document / needs_input /
by_hand / review / blocked) and a plain explanation - reusing `build_general_pack.py`'s own
`VAULT_FILE_FOR` mapping so "already on file" never drifts from what the real pack build checks.
Tested against the whole `templates/general_samples/` corpus (no crashes) and a synthetic bundle;
reuses Finding 40/42's own real fixtures to prove it. Regression-catching verified the same way as
every other fix this session.

**Open questions this raises, not decided here - for Sarel:**
1. Where should a plan live - computed fresh every time the page loads (like `compileReadiness.ts`
   does today, client-side, no DB write), or stored (a new table, so a person's progress on it -
   "I've uploaded the CSD report" - persists and a step can flip from `needs_document` to `ready`)?
2. Should a `needs_input` step (a role, a question) check `tender_answers`/`tender_roles` for an
   already-saved answer on THIS tender, rather than always showing `needs_input`? That needs DB
   access this module deliberately doesn't have yet - a real design choice, not an oversight.
3. Should this run automatically the moment a tender is discovered (before a company commits to
   pursuing it - `compileReadiness.ts`'s own job today, but shallower), or only after pursuit once
   documents are actually downloaded (`build_general_pack.py`'s current precondition)?
4. Should a `needs_input`/`needs_document` step auto-seed a row in `tender_tasks` (the existing
   per-tender task list), or stay a separate read-only view?

**My own recommendation on each, added 2026-10-21 ~19:00 UTC - so this is "approve/override", not
"design from scratch" (still your call, not decided here):**
1. **Computed fresh, no new table.** `compile_plan()` is already a pure function; recomputing it on
   page load is cheap, and it sidesteps inventing a whole new persistence layer. "Progress"
   (#2 below) comes from tables that already exist, not a new one tracking the plan itself -
   avoids exactly the kind of duplicate ad hoc status system the UI/UX review session is
   currently unwinding elsewhere on this same screen cluster (#35/#36, right above).
2. **Yes** - but keep `compile_plan()` itself DB-free. Have the *caller* (an app server action)
   fetch `tender_answers`/`tender_roles` for this tender and fold them into the `company`/`tender`
   dicts passed in, so an already-answered question or a tagged role flips to `ready` without the
   engine module touching Supabase directly - same read/compute split `requirements.py` and
   `build_general_pack.py` already keep.
3. **After pursuit, once documents are downloaded** - matches `build_general_pack.py`'s existing
   precondition, and a real plan needs real document content to mean anything. `compileReadiness.ts`
   can keep doing the shallower pre-pursuit "should we even go for this" job it already does -
   different funnel stage, not a duplicate.
4. **Stay read-only for now.** Auto-seeding one `tender_tasks` row per manifest line could mean
   10+ new tasks appearing per tender the moment a plan is computed, before you've seen whether
   that's wanted at all - narrower to start, matching this project's own "start with a button, not
   the fancier thing" pattern elsewhere (e.g. the Pipeline page's own documented choice). Can widen
   to auto-seeding later once the read-only view has been used for a while.

## Repo shape, in one paragraph

Two independent codebases share this repo: `engine/` (Python, no shared runtime with the web
app — invoked by hand, cron, or the always-on bridge worker (`engine/worker/`), writes to Supabase via the
service-role key, never imported by Next.js) and `app/` (Next.js 16 web app, reads/writes
Supabase directly under RLS). They meet only at the Supabase schema
(`app/supabase/migrations/`, now `0001`–`0026` plus `0030`–`0045`, `0048`, `0050`, `0051`, `0053`, `0054`, `0055`, `0056` (`0046`, `0047`, `0049` claimed by in-flight worktrees at the time of writing); `0027`–`0029` are claimed by other agents' in-flight, not-yet-committed work) and at `config/klipcorp_profile.json`
(gitignored real data; `config/test_companies/*.json` are the committed synthetic stand-ins).
Three buyer-filling/generation engines exist side by side under `engine/`: SANRAL (mature,
root-level scripts), `engine/general/` (non-SANRAL: requirement extraction, SBD/MBD form fill, pack build), and `engine/cv/`
(CV document generator). The CV engine now has two real integration points in `app/`
(upload-mode choice, tender-specific generation request) bridged asynchronously by
`engine/cv/process_cv_jobs.py`. The SANRAL engines now also have one: the whole submission pack
(`engine/pack/`, migration `0017`), bridged by `engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py` the same way. The general engine now has one too (migration
`0018`): Discovery's "Prepare this tender" → a general Tender Workspace → `tender_engine_jobs`,
bridged by `engine/general/process_general_jobs.py`.

## Built and verified — working today

| Area | What it does | How verified |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SANRAL workbook fill (`engine/fill_tender.py`, `fill_conventional.py`, `fill_a_forms.py`, `fill_financial*.py`) | Fills both template families (Conventional 9-sheet, RRM 15-sheet), A-Forms bundle, financial/hours sheets | `engine/admin_harness.py` regression-tests this against 3 test companies on every run; real tender runs recorded in git history (e.g. `afad9d2`, `6658b73`) |
| Template fingerprinting (`engine/fingerprint.py`) | Detects a changed SANRAL template before filling | Documented false-positive case already found and understood (README's own "open question") |
| Field-level provenance (`engine/provenance.py`, migration `0002`) | Every written field tagged confirmed/computed/assumed_default/missing | `app/app/tenders/[id]/page.tsx` reads `field_provenance` directly and renders the 3-bucket readiness report (item 32) — genuinely wired end-to-end, not just a CLI/DB concept |
| National tender discovery (`engine/discovery/etenders_national.py`, `assess_tender.py`, `watch_new_tenders.py`, `company_profiles.py`, `seed_supabase_opportunities.py`) | Pulls OCDS feed; reads each tender's documents once and scores it **separately for every company** (each from its own Experience Library tags, CIDB, B-BBEE, offices - no default/sample profile since 2026-10-17, audit Q4), one `discovered_opportunities` row per company x report-worthy tender with that company's own verdict. Test companies (`is_test_company`) included by default since 2026-10-17 (`--exclude-test-companies`). Seen store: `discovery_seen_releases` (0038, per company x release) in Supabase mode; the local `state/seen_tenders.json` only for a `--profile` run. Since 2026-10-17 (Audit §11): a company whose own profile changed since it was scored (stored `profile_fingerprint` differs) is re-scored and a report-worthy result reported again (`rescored: profile_changed`, `previous_verdict`), its seen row updated in place; an `ERROR` verdict is retried every run and recorded in `system_alerts`. ## In progress / partially built

- **OCR for scanned documents (experimental, 2026-10-17)** — `engine/ocr/scan_ocr.py` (Tesseract 5, local, R0/page, about 3-6 s/page) plugged into `requirements.read_document` (pages with <200 chars of text layer that hold an image) and `extract_cv_fields.read_cv_text` (scanned PDF pages, image uploads). Per-page quality gate; failing pages are refused as before, with the reason. Flagged everywhere: manifest `documents[].ocr` + `from_ocr`, a gap line, the Workspace's blue OCR notice, CV values unticked + OCR banner. Worker image adds `tesseract-ocr(-eng,-osd)`; `OCR_DISABLED=1` switches it off. Measured on the real scans (Tourism NB143, ESKOM annexures + SOW, the B2.1CE certificates) and on text tenders turned into scans (SALB, Dawid Kruiper, Overberg: same manifest apart from overlay → by hand). Known misreads: individual numbers at high confidence ("10HOO", a contract number, a phone number), so it is for finding requirements, not copying values. Not measured: the Claude step on a real OCR'd CV (no API key). Recommendation and removal steps: `docs/specs/OCR-Evaluation.md`.

- **CV AI-extraction** — built end to end (Built table), but it waits on two things Sarel has to provide: an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` on the bridge worker (until then AI-extract uploads stay queued and the `cv_extract` pass logs why), and a first measured run on 3-5 real team CVs. Only the text step has met real CVs so far. Scanned CVs are now OCR'd (experimental, see below): every value read from a scan starts unticked; a scan OCR can't read clearly is still refused.
- **Automatic CV/pack fulfilment** — the worker is built and tested (Built table), but nothing runs it until Sarel deploys it (Railway steps in `Automated-Fulfillment-Deployment.md`). Until then, queued requests wait in `requested`, or someone runs `python3 engine/worker/run_bridges.py --loop` by hand. The pack bridge (`engine/pack/process_pack_jobs.py`) has landed at the path `run_bridges.py` expects, with the same `--once`/`--loop` contract. `run_bridges.py --once --bridge pack` drives it, and the worker Dockerfile now installs Calc + `python3-uno` for it.
- **Role-based digest's `--mode live`** — written, reads the real schema shape, but never run against a live Supabase project (none exists in this environment).

## Known gaps (named, not just "incomplete")

1. **General (non-SANRAL) path: closed as a path, narrowed as automation (2026-10-17).** Flat-PDF MBD/SBD 1, 4, 9 are now typed onto the buyer's printed PDF, as are the CIDB Compulsory Enterprise Questionnaire and the Form of Offer signatory block; tenders not on eTenders go in via the manual load (`/tenders/new`, 0024); the two job tables are one queue (`0026`). Still manual, named in `General-Tender-Preparation-Findings.md` "Gaps": flat MBD/SBD 6.1 and 8; any field the overlay couldn't place safely (listed per form in the pack); the human check of every typed page before signing; the remaining buyer forms (certificate of authority, Record of Addenda, ESKOM Form A / declarations / NEC3, consent forms - prioritised backlog, Round 4 Finding 11); MBD 4 3.9-3.14 and its directors table; the SBD 6.1 points table; scanned tenders are OCR'd only experimentally (see `OCR-Evaluation.md` - tables, white-on-black text and handwriting read badly; flat-PDF typing never offered on OCR'd pages); no CIDB registration-number column.
2. **`admin_harness.py` still only exercises the SANRAL path.** Narrowed: `--pack` now covers the SANRAL submission pack end to end, and the tender-customised CV generation inside it. The general engine now has its own parallel harness (`engine/general/general_harness.py`, 9 real samples x 3 test companies, also in CI as `--no-pack` + `test_general_bridge.py`); the CV generator itself still has none, and two of the three SANRAL fixtures stop at the filler (see Built table). A buyer wording variance or a `people`/`projects` schema change could silently break either and nothing would catch it the way SANRAL template changes are caught.
3. **CV AI-extraction: built, unmeasured.** No API key exists in this environment, so Claude's accuracy on real CVs (including the SANRAL Form B1/B2 grid that is the only real team "CV" in evidence) has never been measured, and the live API has never accepted the exact structured-output schema. Scanned CVs are refused rather than read. Other professional bodies (SAICE, SACAP...) are read but have no column to be saved in. Details: `CV-Extraction-Findings.md` §6/§8.
4. **Test-company coverage is 3 profiles, not 4.** The spec's own item-30 description names a 4th scenario — "no confirmed specialist for a position" — with no matching fixture. Low priority, spec itself calls this an open question.
5. **`is_test_company` exists in the schema; nothing reads or sets it yet.** `engine/admin_harness.py` still reads `config/test_companies/*.json`, not a real company row from Supabase — that's a genuine rewrite needing a live Supabase project to build and verify against, not a column add. No UI sets the flag either. Both are named follow-ups, not silently dropped — full history and sourcing caveats in the pass-history section below.
6. **No `people` storage-path column yet for the original uploaded CV file.** `cv_uploads.storage_path` actually covers this now (see Built table) — this gap from an earlier pass is **resolved**, recorded here only so the history entry below isn't mistaken for still-open.
7. **`tender_requirements`' SETUP facts (managerial flag, tender project type, DS specialism description) are unseeded**, except for tenders whose templates went through the intake (manual load, 2026-10-17), which now get SETUP positions, descriptions and the Man/Non-Man flag written to `tender_requirements` from the uploaded workbook; so the SANRAL score estimate is wider than it needs to be, and every DS1 shows role fit as "Confirm by hand" (a DS role can't be matched to a tag without its specialism). `tenders.evaluation_rules` is also unseeded until `engine/seed_tender_evaluation_rules.py --write` runs against a live project. The vault-field half of this gap (TCS PIN, insurance, ISO, bank-letter date, B-BBEE proof) is **closed** by `0014`. Two related items remain: Klipcorp's ISO 9001 certificate number and expiry are still unknown, and CSD registration validity has no column.
8. **Uploads are capped at ~4.4 MB** (Server Action body `4.5mb`, which is Vercel's hard 413 limit) for CVs, experience and the vault. **Narrowed this pass**: the pattern to fix it now exists and is proven — `app/app/tenders/new/manual-tender-form.tsx` uploads straight from the browser to the `tender-documents` bucket via the Supabase client (`supabase.storage.from(...).upload(...)`, RLS-gated by `manualPrefix()`), never touching a Server Action body at all. That's a real answer to "is it worth building" (the open item below) for one path; the other three (CVs, experience, vault) still go through a capped Server Action and haven't been migrated to this pattern yet.
9. **Narrowed 2026-10-18 (`a232e77`, Sarel's own commit — the first human-authored commit in this whole project): a live Supabase project and a Vercel deployment now exist.** Sarel applied every migration through `0062` to the real project and got a green Vercel build, after fixing three build-breaking issues the sandbox's own `next build` had never caught (no Supabase env vars here means those prerender failures never surfaced locally): `/login` instantiating the Supabase client at component-body top level (fails prerender when env vars aren't visible at build time), `/tools/deadline-calculator` reading `new Date()` during render (Next 16 rejects non-deterministic prerender output), and no `engines.node` pin in `package.json`. All three independently re-verified this pass: `npm run build` now completes cleanly end to end in this sandbox too (29/29 static pages, `/login` and all 3 `/tools/*` routes now genuinely static) — the "`/login`'s pre-existing prerender gap" caveat that every single pass's own build verification has carried all session is gone. **What this changes:** nothing built so far has been tested against real Supabase rows, and this pass still has no live credentials to do that itself — scratch-Postgres replay (now through `0063`) stays the verification method here. What it means going forward: the next person with real project access can actually click through the app, and any gap or bug that was "unverified against live rows" throughout this file can start being closed for real rather than only in a replayed schema. ## This pass (2026-10-29, standing QA/robustness review - one-hundred-and-twenty-third run): Finding 97 (moderate) - a corrupted SANRAL fingerprint baseline file raised a raw JSONDecodeError out of the real intake job instead of the clean "error" status every other failure mode in the same function already reports

Orientation: `git fetch origin main` showed two new sibling commits (`499ae0b` a standing-review
clean sweep across job-queue claims/impersonation/migration 0104/PDF verify, `ee36c9e` a real fix -
`apply_payfast_itn()` moved `current_period_end` forward even on a FAILED payment, migration `0105`
written and pushed but not yet applied to the live DB per the standing rule) - both no overlap. PR
`#172` (Document Vault badge fix) still open/unchanged, TypeScript-only. Other open PRs (`#164`/
`#165`) re-confirmed TS-only.

Rotated to intake. `classify_tender.py` has had two dedicated passes already (Findings 78/90), so
looked specifically for the ONE established pattern not yet checked everywhere: `check_fingerprint()`
wraps `build_fingerprint()` in its own try/except and checks for a missing baseline file, but the
baseline file's own `json.load(open(path))` read had no guard at all - the same asymmetric-guard
shape (one branch handles a failure cleanly, a sibling doesn't) already found and fixed
independently in Findings 82/83/84.

regeneration just replaced one of) raises a raw `JSONDecodeError` straight out of
`check_fingerprint()`. Traced the real consequence: `process_general_jobs.py`'s `process_job()` has

already-anticipated failure mode into a confusing raw-exception message on that one job, instead of
the clear "could not read the stored baseline" text every sibling failure mode already produces.

`build_fingerprint()` two lines above it. **Verified red-then-green**: new test - the first
dedicated test for `check_fingerprint()` at all - covers no-baseline/match/mismatch/corrupted-file;
reverting the fix made only the corrupted-file case fail, exactly as predicted. Restored: `0
failure(s)`. `test_fingerprint.py`/`test_general_bridge.py` re-run clean. Already wired into CI.

Full writeup: Finding 97, `docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md`.

## This pass (2026-10-29, standing QA/robustness review - one-hundred-and-twentieth run): Finding 95 (severe) - a whitespace-only value was reported "placed" on the real Form of Offer/MBD1, its own read-back verification vacuously passing, while the printed page showed nothing at all

Orientation: `git fetch origin main` showed two new sibling commits (`85d5c84`/`4bdf22e`, clean sweep
+ a real `send_digest_emails.py` fix - every digest's "Documents & registrations due" line showed a
raw field name instead of its human label), then a THIRD landed mid-cycle (`e342bae`, naming the
person on a `person_credential` renewal line too) - notify is being actively worked by a sibling
right now, so stayed clear of it again. Open PR `#170` unchanged, still touching
`process_general_jobs.py`/`process_pack_jobs.py`/the fingerprint baseline/Mzansi seed data - avoided
entirely.

Rotated to non-SANRAL pack - genuinely never had a dedicated pass of its own; picked
`engine/general/fill_flat_pdf.py` (1000+ lines, municipal MBD/CIDB flat-PDF form filling) since it
had zero dedicated test file anywhere (only `test_form_field_audit.py` touches it, and only a tiny
slice).

**The finding**: `place_text_fields()`/`place_captions()` both gate "is there a real value to
place" with a bare `if not value:`. A whitespace-only string (a real shape: leading/trailing spaces
from a copy-paste into a name field) is truthy, so it sails past the guard; Helvetica's own space
width is non-zero so `_fit()` "fits" it; the overlay write types invisible blank space; and
`verify_placements()`'s own read-back check strips all whitespace before comparing, so an all-
whitespace value's `want` becomes the empty string - a substring of anything, so it's reported
`verified = True` no matter what's actually on the page. Confirmed end to end against a real
synthetic MBD1 page built with reportlab (not reasoned about in the abstract): the real
`fill_flat_pdf()` reported `{"status": "placed", "value": "   "}` for the contact-person field - the
same `signatory_name`/`signatory_name_upper` path the real Form of Offer's own signatory-name field
uses too.

**Fix:** both guards changed to `if not (value or "").strip():` - rejects whitespace-only as
missing, leaves a real value's own internal/surrounding whitespace untouched. `place_choices()`
checked too and is naturally immune.

**Verified red-then-green against the real pipeline**: new file `test_fill_flat_pdf.py` builds a
real synthetic MBD1 page and runs the real `fill_flat_pdf()`. Reverted the fix: the whitespace-only
and tab/newline-only cases failed exactly as predicted; the unchanged-behaviour cases stayed green
throughout. Restored: `ALL PASSED`, 10/10. `test_form_field_audit.py` re-run clean, no regression.
Wired into CI.

Full writeup: Finding 95, `docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md`.

## This pass (2026-10-28, standing QA/robustness review - one-hundred-and-twelfth run): Finding 89 (severe) - a YAML `.nan`/`.inf` capture value bypassed the Financial Submission hours guard and wrote a non-numeric cell into a real SANRAL workbook; also closed 3 engine/test_*.py CI-wiring gaps, including Finding 81's own regression test

Orientation: `git fetch origin main` showed one new sibling commit (`6930b17`, a standing-review
flag - not fix - of submitted-tender nagging across `send-deadline-reminders.ts`/
`send-returnables-digest.ts`, TypeScript/`scripts/` only, no overlap) - fast-forwarded cleanly. Two
open PRs (`#164`, `#165`), both re-confirmed TypeScript-only via the GitHub API, no `engine/`
overlap.

Rotated to SANRAL pack - last dedicated bug-hunting pass was Finding 81 (run 100, the Form B7
precedence bug), so picked the adjacent, less-reviewed financial-forms code:
`fill_financial_hours.py` (fills the 7 "Hours <Discipline>" sheets of a real Financial Submission
workbook, feeding FORM C2.4 FIN's Workplan Appropriateness score).

**The finding.** A sibling pass (2026-10-24) had already added a guard rejecting a non-numeric/
boolean/negative `hours` value in the capture.yaml - but asked the standard follow-up question for
any numeric guard: does `hours < 0` actually exclude every float a YAML parser can produce? YAML
1.1's `.nan`/`.inf`/`-.inf` literals are valid float syntax PyYAML's `safe_load` parses without
complaint, and `float('nan') < 0` / `float('inf') < 0` are both `False` (IEEE 754 comparison rules)
- so both sailed straight past the guard. Reproduced directly against the real fixture
(`R.334-030-2025.1F_Financial_Submission_ran.xlsm`): the written workbook's real XML held literal
`<v>nan</v>` / `<v>inf</v>` in a numeric cell - not valid per `xsd:double`'s own required
capitalization, feeding a real `ROUND(F8*E8, 2)` formula on a document meant for actual SANRAL
evaluators. `-.inf` was separately confirmed already caught by the existing check (`-inf < 0` is
`True`) - only NaN and positive infinity were the real gap.

**Fix:** `math.isfinite(hours)` added to the guard. Verified red-then-green: reverting the fix made
exactly the 2 predicted new cases fail (not `-.inf`, confirming test precision); restored, full
suite (6 adversarial cases plus the pre-existing valid-value checks) passes clean.

**A third CI-wiring gap, same shape as Findings 87/88, found in the same pass**: swept every
`engine/test_*.py` against `bridge-worker-ci.yml` and found 3 files never wired in -
`test_fill_financial_hours.py` (this finding's own test), `test_fill_b7_legacy_precedence.py`
(Finding 81's OWN regression test, run 100 - missed at the time it was written), and
`test_fill_docx_forms.py`. All 3 confirmed to run clean from the repo root; added as 3 new CI steps.

Full writeup: Finding 89, `docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md`.

## This pass (2026-10-28, standing QA/robustness review - one-hundred-and-eleventh run): Finding 88 (severe) - the pack-ready notification claimed its one-time idempotency token BEFORE checking RESEND_API_KEY was configured, permanently losing a company's "bid pack ready" email if the key happened to be unset at that moment

Orientation: `git fetch origin main` showed one new sibling commit (`db06ad3`, a standing-review
clean sweep of `engine/general/requirements.py` - the non-SANRAL requirement-extraction engine,
no new bug found, no overlap with this pass) - fast-forwarded cleanly before starting. Read the
standing rule at this file's own top (no direct production DB mutations without sign-off) - didn't
apply, no live-database access used this pass. Two open PRs (`#164`, `#165`), both re-confirmed via
the GitHub API to be TypeScript-only, no `engine/` overlap; `#166` (the big Admin Command Center
build-out) already merged by this point.

Rotated to notify - `send_digest_emails.py`/`daily_digest.py` had already had dedicated passes
(coverage closure + live-mode checks), so picked the two files in that area with effectively zero
prior review: `send_pack_ready_email.py` and `record_heartbeat.py`.

**The finding.** `send_pack_ready_email.py`'s own docstring explicitly claims to use "the SAME
notification_claims/record_notification_sent RPCs every TypeScript sender already uses" - checked
whether it actually follows the canonical TypeScript sender's own stated ordering rule
(`app/lib/notificationEngine.ts`'s `sendNotification()`, whose header comment says plainly: check
`RESEND_API_KEY` is configured BEFORE calling `claim_notification()`, specifically because
`notification_claims` is a one-time-only token that claiming-without-sending would permanently
waste). It didn't: the Python sender claimed the token first, unconditionally, and only checked the
key deep inside the per-recipient send loop. Since this job id never fires a second time (nothing
re-invokes the sender once a pack is `"ready"`), a key that happened to be unset at that exact
moment (a staging environment, a key-rotation gap) would permanently lose that company's one-and-
only pack-ready email, even after the key was later configured - the exact bug
`notificationEngine.ts`'s own comment names and was written to avoid.

**Fix:** moved the `RESEND_API_KEY` check to the top of the function, before any claim is made - an
early, un-claimed return when the key is missing, mirroring the canonical sender exactly. A related
test-hygiene gap surfaced while writing the regression test (two pre-existing tests implicitly
depended on this sandbox's own ambient `RESEND_API_KEY` once the check moved earlier) - fixed with
a `setdefault` so the suite is deterministic regardless of ambient state, confirmed by running it
both with and without the sandbox's own key present.

**Verified red-then-green**: new test asserts `claim_notification` is never called with no key
configured; reverting the real fix made it (and one existing test) fail exactly as predicted;
restored: `0 failure(s)`, 11 checks. `engine/general/test_general_bridge.py` - the real integration
path that actually calls this function - re-run clean, `ALL PASSED`.

**A second, independent gap, same shape as Finding 87, fixed in the same pass**: neither
`test_send_pack_ready_email.py` nor `test_record_heartbeat.py` had ever been wired into
`bridge-worker-ci.yml` - confirmed by grep, zero mentions anywhere. Added two new CI steps running
both, after confirming both run clean from the repo root first.

Full writeup: Finding 88, `docs/specs/QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md`.

## This pass (2026-10-27, standing QA/robustness review - one-hundred-and-eighth run): the Lephalale discovery reader's "recent enough to fetch" cutoff used a naive UTC today(), one day too lenient - a proactive repo-wide sweep after Finding 85, same follow-through discipline as the docx_text() sweep two cycles ago

Orientation: synced a sibling commit (`6c4f461`, a clean sweep of the narrative anti-collusion
uniqueness check - `engine/narrative/uniqueness.py`, no overlap; the sibling also flagged that this
routine's own Finding 85 entry landed mid-file rather than at the very top of `System-Status.md`,
same place every one of this routine's entries has always landed - a different, parallel top-of-
file convention another standing routine keeps, not something to change here).

Given Finding 85 was the SIXTH independent occurrence of the naive-UTC-"today" bug class in this
codebase, did a proactive repo-wide grep for the pattern before picking a new rotation area -
found 8 candidates, triaged each by real reachability and stakes rather than fixing every hit
(`suggest_pack.py`/`fingerprint.py`/`harness_pack.py`: informational timestamps only;
`etenders_national.py`: CLI-only, never called by the live path; `gov_sources.py`'s
`"etenders_ocds"` branch: not in the production `ALL_SOURCES`; `process_narrative_jobs.py`'s
years-of-experience calc: real but inert for this bug, `// 365` absorbs a 1-day error on all but
the exact anniversary day; `assemble_pack.py`'s "Generated" footer: cosmetic only).

**Finding 86 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate).** `lephalale.py`'s `_recent_enough()` stood out as the
one candidate that's both a real decision gate (not metadata) and genuinely reachable (`lephalale`
IS in `gov_sources.ALL_SOURCES`, the real daily-discovery default). It computed its cutoff via
naive `datetime.date.today()`, despite already importing `source_http as sh`, which defines the
standard `SAST` constant every sibling reader uses. Worked out the actual DIRECTION of the bug by
hand: a naive UTC "today" one day behind means the cutoff is also one day further back, making the
filter one day MORE lenient, not stricter - the opposite shape from most of this bug class's prior
findings. The practical effect: a batch that should already be excluded as too old is still
fetched for one extra day, during the 00:00-01:59 SAST window - not a tender silently dropped.

**Fix:** reused the already-imported `sh.SAST` - no new constant needed.

**Verified the regression test actually catches the regression - the hard way, again.** The first
version of the new test case repeated Finding 85's exact mistake (only mocked `datetime.datetime`,
not `datetime.date`), and reverting the real fix with only that mock showed `ALL PASSED` at first
(one check happened to agree with the real sandbox clock's actual date). Caught this immediately
with the lesson still fresh, fixed the test to mock both classes to a moment deliberately
different from today's real date. Re-reverted with the corrected test: failed with the exact
predicted wrong verdict; restored: `0 failure(s)`, full suite passing. `test_gov_sources.py`
re-run clean.

Full details: Finding 86 in `QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md`.

## This pass (2026-10-27, standing QA/robustness review - one-hundred-and-seventh run): a real authority-to-sign letter's own {{date}} field could print yesterday's date - the naive-UTC-"today" bug class independently found yet again, this time in company_documents.py

Orientation: synced two sibling commits (`2ee1e9c` real `tenderCompliance.ts` SACNASP-regex fix,
`b3bd916` a flagged-not-fixed `dispatchDashboard.ts` over-triggering question - both app/TypeScript
only, no overlap). Three open PRs (`#164`/`#165`/`#166`), all read by the sibling passes, confirmed
not touching anything here.

Rotated to SANRAL pack (most overdue by this routine's own numbered rotation). Read
`fill_authority_letter.py` and its real logic in `company_documents.py` end to end. This exact
codebase has independently found and fixed the naive-UTC-"today" bug class in `fill_a_forms.py`,
`fill_sbd_docx.py`'s own `_today_iso()`, `watch_deadlines.py`'s closing-day math and `pdf_merge.py`'s
`expiry_warning()` - each its own separate finding, never a shared root fix - so worth checking
whether `authority_facts()`'s own independent "today" computation had made the identical mistake.

**Finding 85 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate).** It had. `authority_facts()`'s `"date"` field (a real,
documented `{{date}}` field a company can mark in its own authority-to-sign letter guideline) used
naive `datetime.date.today()` with no SAST adjustment at all - confirmed by grep that this file,
unlike every sibling (`fill_a_forms.py`/`watch_deadlines.py`/`generate_cv.py`/`source_http.py`),
defines no `SAST` constant. A bridge worker container runs in UTC by default, so this prints
YESTERDAY's date on a real legal document during the 00:00-01:59 SAST window every day. Reproduced
directly by monkeypatching the clock.

**Why the existing test suite never caught it**: `test_company_documents.py`'s guideline case
exercises `{{date}}`, but its own expected-value comparison calls the SAME buggy function a second
time, live, so both sides always agreed regardless of correctness - the bug could only be exposed
by comparing against an independently-injected date, which no existing case did.

**Fix:** added the standard `SAST = datetime.timezone(datetime.timedelta(hours=2))` constant and
switched to `datetime.datetime.now(SAST).date()`.

**Verified the regression test actually catches the regression - the hard way.** The first attempt
at the new test only patched `datetime.datetime`, not `datetime.date` - which let a REVERTED
(buggy) version pass anyway, since the still-live `datetime.date.today()` fell through to the real
sandbox clock, which happened to already read the test's own target date by coincidence. Caught
this by actually reverting and re-running rather than trusting the first green result; rewrote the
test to patch both classes to a moment deliberately different from today's real date. Re-reverted
with the corrected test: failed with the exact predicted wrong date; restored: `0 failure(s)`,
full suite passing. `test_form_field_audit.py` (the sibling SAST-date tests for the other two
files) re-run clean.

Full details: Finding 85 in `QA-Edge-Case-Findings.md`.

## This pass (2026-10-26, standing QA/robustness review - one-hundred-and-second run): a legacy .doc whose LibreOffice conversion produced a broken file raised an uncaught exception straight out of the document reader shared by discovery, intake and general-pack extraction

Orientation: synced a sibling commit (`3ade4a0`, a standing-review pass giving real review to two
self-merged PRs - #159's dashboard-stats tenant leak fix, confirmed sound; #163's new discovery
`.docx`/`.doc` fallback reader, confirmed sound by running its own test suite). No open PRs.

wiring an existing function into a new caller is exactly the shape this routine's own history

while real and direct - checked the PR's own claims, not adversarial edge cases against the
shared function it now exposes to a new caller.

**Finding 82 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, moderate).** `requirements.py`'s `read_document()` - shared by the
new discovery fallback, manual intake, and general-pack extraction - guards its `fmt == "docx"`
branch's `docx_text()` call with a `try/except` ("corrupt / not really a docx") but not its

inside its thread pool, so this degrades to a generic `"ERROR"` verdict + a `system_alerts` entry
for that one tender rather than crashing the whole daily run - real, but moderate, not severe.

**Fix:** wrapped `docx_text(conv)` in the same `try/except` pattern the sibling `docx` branch
already uses, naming the conversion (not python-docx generically) as the problem.

**Verified red, then green:** new case added to the sibling's own `test_document_reader_fallback.py`

## This pass (2026-10-26, standing QA/robustness review - one-hundredth run): a company's explicit "Form B7 is waived" answer could be silently overridden by a stale legacy Targeted Enterprise, writing a false subcontracting declaration into the real submitted SANRAL workbook

collision; a WhatsApp widget feature; a merged tender-workspace wiring PR - all `app/`/

## This pass (2026-10-24, standing QA/robustness review - eighty-sixth run): a tender closing near midnight SAST could report its own closing day as one real day late, in a customer-facing compliance reminder

Orientation: synced two sibling landings since the last run - PR #144 (Operational Notification
Engine, TypeScript-only: `sent_operational_alerts`/migration `0092`/`scripts/send-operational-alerts.ts`,
no `engine/` files touched, confirmed by diff) and a documented cross-session collision on that
same feature, resolved by direct coordination before either side pushed conflicting work - neither
affects this pass. Rotated to compliance/reminders - the most overdue standing area (last dedicated
pass the seventy-eighth run, 2026-10-23).

**Finding 72 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe).** `find_documents_lapsing_before_closing()`'s own comment
says it computes "calendar day in SAST, like app/lib/dates.ts closingDayOf()" - checked that claim
against the real TypeScript rather than trusting it. `closingDayOf()` normalizes to an absolute UTC
instant FIRST, then adds 2h (correct for any input offset, since JS's `Date` always normalizes).
The Python port instead added the 2h directly to the still-timezone-AWARE parsed value - which only
shifts wall-clock fields while keeping the ORIGINAL offset attached, a different operation that's
only correct when the input happens to already be UTC. Confirmed `tenders.closing_date` genuinely
carries BOTH conventions in real data: `gov_sources.iso_sast()` and `process_general_jobs.py`'s own
SANRAL intake tag it "+02:00" (SAST); `watch_tender_updates.apply_closing_date()` writes whatever a
raw OCDS feed gives, genuine UTC. For a "+02:00" value between 22:00-23:59 SAST, the bug rolled the
calculated closing day one real day late - confirmed directly
(`"2026-10-22T23:00:00+02:00"`, real day the 22nd, came back as the 23rd). The existing test for
this exact function only ever used "+00:00" fixtures, so this never surfaced despite being
reachable from two real write paths, and the wrong date is shown directly in a customer-facing
compliance reminder's own `closing_date` field.

**Fix:** `closing_day` now converts to UTC (`closing_ts.astimezone(datetime.timezone.utc)`) before
adding the 2-hour SAST shift, matching `closingDayOf()`'s own normalize-then-shift order.

**Verified the regression test actually catches the regression:** new
`closing_day_handles_a_sast_tagged_offset_correctly()` in `test_watch_deadlines_urgency.py` (a
"+02:00"-tagged closing time at 23:00 SAST). Reverted the fix: the reported date came back one real
day late, exactly as predicted; restored: `0 failures`. Every other compliance/notify suite that
touches this module re-run clean.

## This pass (2026-10-24, standing QA/robustness review - eighty-fifth run): a broken formula in a buyer's BOQ workbook could be silently read as a confirmed zero rate/amount, not an unknown value

Orientation: rotated to discovery - the most overdue standing area - but checked `git log`/open
branches first and found live, uncollided in-flight work on PR #141 (`tender-workspace-batch-2b`)
touching several discovery reader files (`kouga.py`/`lephalale.py`/`randwater.py`/
`vaal_central_water.py`/`source_http.py`/`assess_tender.py`, plus one block of
`process_general_jobs.py`'s closing-time default) - deliberately avoided all of those per the
standing "never overwrite another agent's in-flight work" rule, and picked a different, untouched
corner of the same area instead: `engine/discovery/boq_extraction.py`, the brand-new real BOQ
line-item parser (the same feature whose missing `lxml` dependency broke both daily cron workflows
earlier today - under heavy scrutiny today for an unrelated reason, good odds something else in it
hadn't been looked at this closely yet).

**Finding 71 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe).** `sanral_fill.Workbook`'s two cell decoders (`cached()`,
`_decode_cell_value()`) treat a literal string formula result (`t="str"`) and a FORMULA ERROR
(`t="e"` - `#DIV/0!`, `#REF!`, etc.) identically. Of the standard Excel error codes, `#DIV/0!` is
the only one containing a literal digit - `award_outcomes.parse_rand()` (reused by
`boq_extraction.py` for every quantity/rate/amount cell) strips everything but digits before
parsing, so every OTHER error code correctly returns `None`, but `#DIV/0!` strips to `"0"` and
parses to the float `0.0`. Confirmed end to end with a real, minimal `.xlsx`: a BOQ row with a
genuinely broken Rate/Amount formula (dividing by a blank cell, a completely realistic real-world
case) came back from the real `parse_boq_workbook()` as `rate_zar: 0.0, amount_zar: 0.0` -
indistinguishable from a confirmed, genuinely free line item.

**Fix:** both decoders now return `None` for `t="e"`, instead of grouping it with `t="str"`. No
other code anywhere in this repo relies on an error-cell's string value (confirmed by grep before
touching this shared class).

**Verified the regression test actually catches the regression:** new
`test_formula_error_cell_is_null_not_a_fabricated_zero()` in `test_boq_extraction.py`, plus a small
`ExcelError` marker added to that file's own in-memory `.xlsx` builder so a test can represent a
real error-typed cell. Reverted the fix: both new checks failed exactly as predicted (`0.0` instead
of `None`); restored: `0 failures`. Every other test touching `Workbook` in this repo
(`test_sanral_b7.py`, `test_classify_tender.py`, `test_fill_financial_hours.py`,
`test_form_field_audit.py`, `test_tender_enrichment.py`, `test_tender_enrichment_cli.py`) re-run
clean.

## 2026-10-24 ~09:50 UTC addendum - real production break, caught while checking this pass's own CI: both daily cron workflows had been silently dead since this morning

**What happened:** while confirming Finding 70's CI (below) went green, noticed `daily-digest.yml`
run 5 (08:24 UTC) and `daily-discovery.yml` run 2 (07:36 UTC) - both real scheduled runs against
the real Supabase project, not test CI - had `conclusion: failure`. Both were green the day before
(run 4, 2026-10-23). Root cause, identical in both: `engine/discovery/gov_sources.py`'s own
`attach_scope_enrichment()` (part of the real BOQ/scope extraction engine that landed since these
two workflows were last written) added a new, unconditional import chain -
`tender_enrichment.py -> boq_extraction.py -> sanral_fill.py -> \`from lxml import etree\`` -
that nobody updated either workflow for. Both failed with the identical
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'lxml'`:
- `daily-digest.yml`: inside `fetch_releases()`, after a ~14-minute feed read, right before the
  final `digest_report.json` write - that day's digest build never completed for anyone (0 people
  were opted in at the time, so no actual email was lost today, but the next person to opt in
  would have silently gotten nothing).
- `daily-discovery.yml`: inside `gov_sources.fetch_all()`, near the start of the run - the
  **entire discovery pass** (the one job that populates every company's own Discovery page) never
  ran at all today.

`bridge-worker-ci.yml`'s own CI never caught this because it already installs the full
`engine/worker/requirements.txt` (`python-docx` pulls `lxml` in transitively) before running
`test_gov_sources.py` - these two real cron workflows have their own, separate, minimal
"nothing to install" setup (deliberately, per each workflow's own comment, written before this
import chain existed) and were never updated when it did.

**Fix:** added one `pip install lxml==6.1.3` step to each workflow (pinned to the version already
verified elsewhere in this repo) - `lxml` alone, not the whole `python-docx` that normally pulls
it in, since neither script otherwise touches `python-docx`. Reproduced the exact failure in
isolation (blocked the `lxml` import, got the identical `ModuleNotFoundError`), confirmed the
import chain resolves cleanly with it installed. Commits `1e1580e` (daily-digest.yml), `d867e7a`
(daily-discovery.yml).

**Not done unilaterally, flagged for Sarel:** both fixes will take effect on tomorrow's scheduled
runs (daily-discovery 02:45 UTC, daily-digest 03:45 UTC) automatically. Today's discovery pass
never ran at all - whether to manually re-run it now (via `workflow_dispatch`, which its own
docstring says is safe/idempotent) to recover today's data, versus just letting tomorrow's
scheduled run catch up, is Sarel's call, not run unilaterally here: `daily-discovery.yml` writes
to the real database and real Storage, and `daily-digest.yml`'s last step sends real email via
Resend if anyone is opted in by the time it's next run.

## This pass (2026-10-24, standing QA/robustness review - eighty-second run): a SANRAL addendum correcting a typo'd NRA reference could be outvoted by the stale number simply because it's repeated more often on Book 1's own page footer

Orientation: synced a sibling session's merge (`c1fb95b`, PR #137, TypeScript-only Market
Intelligence chart fix - no collision). Rotated to `engine/intake` - the most overdue area in the
standing rotation (last dedicated pass the seventy-fourth run, 2026-10-23). Finding 61 (that run)
and Finding 68 (seventy-ninth run) both fixed the same "plain first-match silently picks a
filename-order winner" bug class elsewhere in this module - worth checking whether a third field
in the same file still had the unflagged version.

**Finding 70 (CONFIRMED, FIXED, severe).** `find_nra_reference()` doesn't even use first-match -
it returns whichever NRA number is MOST FREQUENT across the documents read, with no ambiguity
signal at all (a bare string or `None`, unlike its two siblings). That's worse than a sort-order
coin-flip: SANRAL's NRA reference is often repeated many times over on Book 1's own running page
footer, while a real addendum correcting a typo in it is realistically mentioned only once -
repetition count is actively anti-correlated with which value is actually correct. Confirmed
directly: a synthetic Book 1 footer repeating "NRA: 2026/0071" 8 times plus a single addendum line
correcting it to "NRA: 2026/0017" - the function returned the stale, already-wrong number, with
nothing anywhere aware two different numbers existed. This reference feeds the real envelope
covers and authority letter SANRAL requires and is stored directly on `tenders.nra_reference`.

**Fix:** same shape as Finding 61/68 - `find_nra_reference()` now returns
`{"value": "NRA ...", "ambiguous": bool}` (or `None`), most-frequent value unchanged as the
default, `ambiguous` set when more than one distinct number was found. Updated the one real call
site in `process_general_jobs.py`: the plain-text DB column gets `nra["value"]`; the intake
record's notes gain an extra sentence when `ambiguous` is set.

**Verified the regression test actually catches the regression:** extended
`test_form_field_audit.py::test_intake_readers()` with the single-mention, no-match, and real
outvoting cases. Reverted the fix (keeping the new tests): both new checks failed exactly as
predicted; restored: `0 failures`. `test_classify_tender.py` and `test_process_general_jobs.py`
re-run clean.

## This pass (2026-10-24, standing QA/robustness review - eightieth run): a human-typed typo in fill_financial_hours.py's own capture file could silently corrupt a real SANRAL financial workbook's fee formula

Orientation: rotated to SANRAL pack - most overdue literal rotation slot (last dedicated run was

reachable "silently wrong data" bug on a scored evaluation form and the tendered fee itself.

(name the field and the actual value) anything that isn't a real non-negative `int`/`float`,
